Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the call this morning. NimbusTech is progressing through procurement and we had a few narrow follow-ups from our privacy team about Redwood's role under CCPA/CPRA and how telemetry and edge routing are handled. We've attached a short list of questions and a redline of your standard DPA (attached: NimbusTech_DPA_redline.docx).

Top asks from our counsel:
- Can you confirm Redwood will accept a "service provider" (processor) role under CPRA/CCPA for the Nimbus integration for the covered use cases we discussed (inference-only, no model training, no re-selling of personal data)?
- We need a commitment that telemetry used for operations (latency metrics, aggregated error rates, UUID-based traces) will be limited-purpose. Will you accept explicit telemetry definitions and limited-use language?
- Nimbus operates in CA and routes traffic through CDNs and regional edge points. Does routing telemetry or ephemeral connection metadata that traverses state boundaries count as a transfer that would break the SP classification? If so, what contractual language limits that risk?
- Please provide your current subprocessor list and an ETA for when you can furnish SOC2 documentation and evidence of encryption in transit between Redwood and third-party CDNs.

If you can reply with short, redline-ready language we can circulate internally. We are on a tight timeline and procurement would like to close the commercial terms this month.

Appreciate it,

Karthik / Marissa —

I've reviewed Nimbus's redline and their questions. Below are two pieces: (A) short, redline-ready DPA insert we can propose to maintain "Service Provider" status under CPRA/CCPA; (B) recommended operational commitments (for procurement) on telemetry and routing. I'm attaching a one-page doc with the clause and clean/track changes: redwood_service-provider-suggestion.docx.

(A) Suggested contract language (high level):
"Service Provider; Limited Use. For the purposes of the California Consumer Privacy Act and the California Privacy Rights Act (collectively, CPRA), and similar US state privacy laws, Contractor (Redwood) shall act solely as a Service Provider with respect to Customer Personal Information provided for the delivery of inference services. Contractor shall process Personal Information only on Customer's documented instructions and for the limited purposes set forth in the Agreement (to provide inference services, maintain service health, and for fraud prevention and system security). Contractor shall not retain, use, or disclose Personal Information for any purposes unrelated to performance of the Agreement, including for commercial re‑use or sale."

(B) Telemetry & Routing operational commitments (suggested):
- Telemetry definition: "Telemetry" means aggregated operational metrics, performance traces, anonymized error logs, and ephemeral connection metadata strictly limited to debugging, latency optimization, and service health monitoring. Telemetry excludes persistent identifiers that allow re‑identification of consumers beyond session TTL unless Customer explicitly permits retention in writing.
- Limited use: Telemetry will be used only to operate and improve the service and will not be monetized or shared outside the Service Provider ecosystem except to authorized subprocessors under contract.
- Routing / interstate transit: Temporary routing of encrypted connection metadata through intermediate edge locations or CDNs located in different US states for performance or redundancy shall not, by itself, constitute a transfer of Personal Information for purposes of changing the Service Provider designation, provided that: (i) data is encrypted in transit; (ii) no persistent storage or materialization of Personal Information occurs at the intermediate location beyond cache/TTL; and (iii) Redwood maintains a registry of such routing endpoints and provides Customer with notice and a reasonable opportunity to object for specific jurisdictions.
- Subprocessors & evidence: Redwood will provide NimbusTech with a current list of subprocessors and SOC 2 Type II report on a rolling basis (in advance of production go‑live where possible).

Risks / ask: if Nimbus insists that any interstate CDN hop is treated as a transfer requiring additional contractual guarantees, that introduces operational complexity and potential cost. We can offer additional certification/controls for specific dataflows (e.g., CA-only endpoints) but need procurement to accept an availability/latency tradeoff or a scoped exception.

Next steps: I recommend we propose the language above to Nimbus as a clean-mark with a short cover note and an offer to provide SOC2 artifacts within 5 business days. I'll attach the redline.
